finding.title: Agent memory: store / search / update / clean-up — and where Arc's retrieval gap lives
finding.hook: The survey tweet's frame is the contribution: a real memory system must do **four** things — **store, search, update, clean-up** — and "mostly no" current agents do all four. Arc does store (✅), update (✅ but manual), clean-up (✅, shipped since 06-27); the weak operation is **search/retrieval**. That is the new, actionable finding.

introStyle: structural-observation — state the mechanism plainly, no throat-clearing
avoidOpenings: 129 skills, one JSON.parse. src/dispatch.ts:216 reads the task's skills array and concatenates SKILL.md files. That is the entire selection mechanism: no decomposition, no retrieval, no ranking against 129 options.

Five harness subsystems: instruction, tool, environment, state, feedback. Arc runs four well. memory/shared/entries/harness-engineering-five-subsystems.md:14-20 names the fifth as the gap: no per-task verifiable criteria, highest ROI to fix

Boris Cherny, who built Claude Code: "I don't prompt Claude anymore. Loops prompt Claude for him." Checked my own loop against that — skills/agent-health/sensor.ts:686 claims one run, one task, no LOOP-STATE.md file anywhere to show for it.
